---
title: "FAIR Research Software Checklist"
subtitle: "A quick self-assessment across all ten uplifting topics"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 2
---

## 1. [Repositories, registries & archiving](topics/1repositories.qmd)

- [ ] Source code is in a public repository (GitHub/GitLab)
- [ ] The repository has a README and an open-source license (MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD 3-Clause, GPL-3.0, …)
- [ ] The license is compatible with the licenses of all dependencies (copyleft, unlicensed, non-commercial)
- [ ] Releases are archived with a persistent identifier (e.g. Zenodo, linked to GitHub)
- [ ] The software is listed in a registry (Research Software Directory, bio.tools, …)

## 2. [Testing](topics/2testing.qmd)

- [ ] Automated tests cover the most critical functions
- [ ] Tests run automatically in CI on every push and pull request
- [ ] Tests live in a dedicated `tests/` directory that mirrors `src/`
- [ ] A test is added with every bug fix and every new feature

## 3. [Software engineering quality](topics/3software_engineering_quality.qmd)

- [ ] The project layout is consistent (`src/`, `tests/`, `docs/`, `examples/`, LICENSE, README, configuration)
- [ ] Code uses descriptive names, guard clauses, and focused functions, without commented-out dead code
- [ ] Changes are reviewed by a person, supported by linters and static analysis
- [ ] Code is improved incrementally as part of everyday work
- [ ] Dependencies are pinned and periodically updated
- [ ] Maintenance status is stated in the README (e.g. a repostatus.org badge)

## 4. [Documentation](topics/4documentation.qmd)

- [ ] Documentation addresses users, deployers, and developers
- [ ] The README covers description, installation, usage, citation, license, and contributing
- [ ] Installation and usage commands work exactly as written
- [ ] Dependencies, environment setup, external services, and configuration are documented
- [ ] A `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers architecture, development setup, running tests, and review expectations
- [ ] Functions have docstrings, and API documentation is generated from them (Sphinx / Read the Docs)

## 5. [Versioning & packaging](topics/5version_control_and_packaging.qmd)

- [ ] Versions follow semantic versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`)
- [ ] Each release is a git tag and a GitHub Release with release notes
- [ ] The software is packaged for its ecosystem (PyPI, CRAN/Bioconductor, npm, …)
- [ ] Pushing a version tag triggers CI to build, publish, and archive the release

## 6. [Demo environment](topics/6demo_environment.qmd)

- [ ] A container definition exists (Docker / Apptainer)
- [ ] The demo runs without local setup (Binder, Colab, Codespaces, Hugging Face Spaces)
- [ ] The demo includes example data and an end-to-end walkthrough notebook or script
- [ ] The demo is pinned to a recent release and updated as part of every release

## 7. [Graphical user interface](topics/7GUI.qmd)

- [ ] You have deliberately decided whether a GUI is worth building
- [ ] The chosen technology matches your effort budget (ipywidgets, Streamlit, Gradio, Shiny, Tkinter/Qt)
- [ ] The GUI is a thin layer that calls the same functions as the CLI or library
- [ ] The GUI has clear labels, sensible defaults, helpful error messages, and guided steps

## 8. [Interoperability](topics/8interoperability.qmd)

- [ ] Data uses open, standard formats (CSV/Parquet, JSON/YAML, HDF5/NetCDF/Zarr, FASTA/FASTQ/VCF)
- [ ] The command-line interface follows conventions: stdin/stdout, `--help`/`--version`, non-zero exit code on failure
- [ ] APIs follow REST conventions and publish an OpenAPI specification
- [ ] Interfaces are described with machine-readable metadata (CodeMeta, EDAM)
- [ ] The tool fits into workflow managers: clear inputs and outputs, no interactive prompts or hidden state

## 9. [Improving workflows](topics/9improving_workflows.qmd)

- [ ] Manual steps are replaced by an executable pipeline (Make, Snakemake, Nextflow, CWL)
- [ ] Each step has well-defined inputs and outputs, with no manual actions in between
- [ ] Each run's provenance is recorded: inputs, code version, parameters (execution reports, W3C PROV, RO-Crate)
- [ ] The pipeline runs automatically (CI, on a schedule, or on HPC) rather than by hand

## 10. [Citation](topics/10citations.qmd)

- [ ] The repository contains an up-to-date `CITATION.cff` (authors, version, DOI)
- [ ] Each release is archived with its own DOI (Zenodo)
- [ ] The repository contains a `codemeta.json` with machine-readable metadata
- [ ] Identifiers are consistent: an ORCID for every author, and the same DOI, repository URL, and version everywhere

```{=html}
<p><button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-secondary btn-sm" id="checklist-reset">Clear all checkboxes</button></p>

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  var key = "fair-checklist";
  var boxes = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("ul.task-list input[type=checkbox]"));
  var saved = {};
  try { saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(key)) || {}; } catch (e) {}

  function save() {
    var state = {};
    boxes.forEach(function (box) { if (box.checked) state[box.dataset.item] = true; });
    try { localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(state)); } catch (e) {}
  }

  boxes.forEach(function (box) {
    box.disabled = false;
    box.dataset.item = box.closest("li").textContent.trim();
    box.checked = !!saved[box.dataset.item];
    box.addEventListener("change", save);
  });

  document.getElementById("checklist-reset").addEventListener("click", function () {
    boxes.forEach(function (box) { box.checked = false; });
    save();
  });
});
</script>
```
